scope: Rewrite GCWeb topic page doormat link text and descriptions.

rules.text: Rewrite the complete doormat set together. Do not optimize one doormat in isolation if that would create inconsistent title style, description style, ordering, or duplicate descriptions across the set.

Return updated HTML for the complete doormat set. When the input is a full HTML page, return the full page HTML with only the doormat section changed and preserve unrelated content exactly as provided.
Preserve each original href unless the user explicitly asks to change destinations.
Preserve existing valid doormat structure. Only repair structure when the issue report identifies a structure problem or the user asks for HTML repair.
Use descriptive link text. Prefer action verbs or concise keywords that summarize the information or tasks available on the destination page.
Keep link text under 75 characters. Aim for 35 characters or fewer when possible.
Use sentence case, no trailing punctuation, and one grammatical style across the doormat set.
Use the description to help users decide whether the link is relevant. Add information not already present in the link text.
Keep descriptions under 120 characters. Aim for fewer than 100 characters when possible.
Prefer concise comma-separated keywords or task phrases. Use one description style across the set.
Do not start descriptions with filler phrases such as Includes, Information on, Learn more about, or Find information about.
Do not reuse identical or near-identical descriptions across doormats. Make each description specific to its destination.
Descriptions must be plain text only: no links, bold text, bullets, or markup inside the paragraph.
Do not end descriptions with punctuation.
Do not leave generic placeholder link text or descriptions. Only include doormats that are customized from the supplied content or user instructions.
